text:
alex: Heads-up: planning a ~3hr rolling node drain in eu-west1-az1 tomorrow 02:00-05:00 UTC to apply NIC firmware + netpol changes. Affects GPU serving pools (p100/rtx).

kate: What exactly changes in the netpol? Will it drop client egress to some destinations?

alex: netpol will tighten egress to internal mgmt subnets and block a few legacy monitoring IP ranges. No customer-facing ingress changes. We need to restart kube-proxy on each node (kernel module reload) which forces a drain/reboot.

sam: Rough blast radius? How many nodes / GPUs?

alex: ~18 nodes, ~72 GPUs across two racks. Rolling per-node drain, 1 node at a time, 10–15m drain + 8–12m reboot + 5–10m validation. Expect 30–40m per rack due to sequencing.

mateo_oncall: Oncall notes: set CUTOFF=01:50 UTC so active long calls get a 10m heads-up. Can we cordon nodes early?

alex: Yes will cordon 10m prior to drain. Plan: cordon -> evict pods (preferentially move to other pools) -> apply firmware -> reboot -> uncordon -> run smoke checks.

julia_cs: Any potential customer impact? We should notify customers using Dedicated pools in eu-west1. Some low-latency jobs may see brief queuing.

alex: Good call — CS notify draft below. Also toggle routing policy to prefer eu-west2 for high-SLA tenants during the window.

infra-bot: scheduled_maintenance created: id=mt-az1-2026-07-05-02, window=2026-07-05T02:00:00Z-2026-07-05T05:00:00Z

kate: What about autoscaler behavior? We should disable autoscale-up on target pools so drains don't trigger extra spin-up events that compete for capacity.

sam: Agree. And add a soft cap on burst so we don't spill into spot nodes unexpectedly.

alex: Action items:
- Disable autoscale-burst on pool-gpu-az1 during window (sam)
- Push netpol change to canary in az1-inner first (kate)
- CS email + workspace banner (julia_cs)
- Oncall standby (mateo_oncall)

kate: Canary plan: apply netpol to 2 nodes, monitor for 20m (connection timeouts, metrics delta), then proceed. Netpol diff below:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tighten-egress-mgmt
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.10.0.0/16
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    except:
    - 203.0.113.0/24    # legacy monitoring
```

mateo_oncall: Will add runbook steps in the incident channel. If any node shows >5% pod eviction failures, abort and rollback netpol.

sam: Cost note: cross-region rerouting to eu-west2 will incur egress charges for some long-running workloads and may increase token compute cost due to higher latency for model shards. Estimate: up to $800 for the window in worst case. Approve?

alex: Approve for this window. We prefer stability. Record the charge in the next infra spend report.

julia_cs: Draft notify (short): "Planned maintenance in eu-west1 (AZ1) on 2026-07-05 02:00–05:00 UTC. Some Dedicated customers may see briefly queued requests or routing to eu-west2. No data plane changes expected. Contact cs@redwood.ai for issues." Thoughts?

mateo_oncall: Add line: "Engineering on call will monitor and rollback if errors >0.5% per route"

kate: Preflight checklist (to run 1hr before):
- Verify spare capacity in eu-west2 (sam)
- Snapshot node labels and taints (alex)
- Bake new kube-proxy image with netpol (kate)
- Confirm infra-bot schedule and slack banner (julia_cs)

alex: I'll run node drain command sequence in prod runbook. Example: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-23
kubectl drain gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --timeout=10m
# run firmware apply script
ssh node-23 sudo ./apply-nic-fw.sh
sudo reboot
```

sam: Leave a 30m stall between racks to let autoscaler normalize.

infra-bot: reminder posted 60m before window

julia_cs: I'll post to workspace and start customer emails 3h before window.

mateo_oncall: I'll be online for the window. If anything funky, escalate to eng-sre.

alex: OK launching canary at 2026-07-05T01:15Z. Will post updates here. :rocket: 

sam: flagging billing team to expect ~1k incremental egress cost, tagging @finance in case they want to pre-approve.

kate: one more: ensure that model version pinning doesn't block evictions (some long-running GPU pods have restartPolicy Never). We need eviction sidecar check.

alex: noted — I'll run a quick query to list pods with restartPolicy=Never in pool-gpu-az1.

julia_cs: thanks team. Keep noise low during the window please.

mateo_oncall: 1796352620 - post-window: all nodes back, smoke checks green, no elevated errors. Rolling close.
